title: The life cycle, reviewed
hookLine: from the adhan in the ear to the last prayer

lines: A CALL WHISPERED IN A NEWBORN'S EAR.
A PRAYER WITH NO CALL BEFORE IT.
cards: A grandfather leans over a newborn, hours old, and whispers the call to prayer into the baby's right ear. Allahu akbar. The baby isn't going to stand up and pray.
There's no prayer after this call. Long afterward, rows of people stand in a mosque courtyard for a funeral prayer. There's no call before that prayer.
Some Muslims put the two together in a saying people repeat: a life is the space between a call and its prayer. Today, the life cycle, from the adhan in the ear to the last prayer.

teach.h: A CALL, A NAME, A TASTE OF DATE.
teach.b: A report in Abu Dawud's collection, in paraphrase, says the Prophet, peace be upon him, gave the call to prayer in the ear of his grandson Hasan when he was born.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, a companion brings his newborn son to the Prophet, who names him, chews a date, and touches it to the baby's mouth.
A good name, a taste of sweetness, and in some families a sacrifice shared in thanks. Then childhood.

teach.h: CHILDREN LEARN BY PRAYING BESIDE YOU.
teach.b: A report in Abu Dawud tells parents to have their children pray from the age of seven: learning by doing, beside the people who love them.

Marriage and home: the year called the nikah a contract of mercy, with consent, witnesses, and a gift to the bride that belongs to her alone, which the Qur'an tells husbands to give, in paraphrase. Illness and death.

teach.h: VISIT THE SICK; SAY THE WORDS OF RETURN.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet tells his followers to feed the hungry, visit the sick and free the captive. A sick room is a place to go toward, not to avoid.
At a loss, the Qur'an gives the words people say: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." Then the funeral prayer, said standing, in rows, for someone who can no longer stand.
Customs differ between cultures and schools at every step. But the shape stays: every stage has its words, and every stage has people around it.

how: Muslim families mark each stage with practices drawn from hadith and local custom: the call to prayer in a newborn's ear, naming and the 'aqiqah, teaching children to pray, the nikah contract, visiting the sick, and washing, shrouding and praying the funeral prayer for the dead.

games.q: a companion brings his newborn son to the Prophet. what happens next?
o: the Prophet names him and touches a chewed date to his mouth.
the Prophet sends him home until the boy is older.
the Prophet asks the father to fast first.
games.why: Sahih al-Bukhari: a name and a taste of sweetness, at the very start of a life.

practice: Walk the stages slowly, one person at each, a new baby you know of, a child learning, a couple, someone sick right now, someone who has died, and give each a few breaths.

If you pray, ask good for each of them in your own words; if you don't, simply hold each face in mind. And if a loss feels too heavy to carry alone, in the US call or text 988, any hour, or elsewhere, local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: The life cycle. From the call in a newborn's ear to the funeral prayer, each stage with its own words and its own people. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a funeral, the word in salat al-janazah, the funeral prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: every stage. From the first call to the last prayer. Rest well.
